assessment.basis: The spec (status: approved design, 2026-10-11) and the plan were read in full. Neither has a draft, obsolete or superseded marker. The plan's last commit 8f2b6ef appends the acceptance results. Both documents cover one feature in two parts: the network gateway and the Hermes Tasks widget. Implementation commits map to plan Tasks 1-9 (ev-commits); the symbols and files named in the plan exist in the working tree. The only recorded verification is the acceptance section (ev-acceptance), which predates commits f66f225, 6accb6a and c5892fd (ev-post-acceptance) and later commits that change the gateway and widget (ev-later-commits). No code review is recorded. Source grep for credential-like terms found only test fixtures and design text, no secrets. Archive mode is incomplete-evidence by explicit user request.

evidence.summary: Approved design. Part 1 network gateway: network permission, per-package exact-origin allowlist, http.get (confirm never) and http.send (confirm optional), no redirects, 4 s upstream timeout, 100 KB body, 120 KB answer, no secrets. Part 2 Hermes Tasks widget in examples/widgets/hermes-tasks: views, tags, complete/skip/undo, reschedule, autosave edits, quick add, 10 s polling, theme tokens only. Out of scope: secrets, streaming and binary bodies, recurrence editing, archive, project management.

Ten tasks. Tasks 1-9 implement the gateway and widget with one commit each. Task 10 is full verification and browser acceptance, with results appended under «Acceptance results (2026-10-11)». The plan's Task 9 quick add uses a form submit handler.

scope.text: Manifest network field and network permission, with origin validation and normalization (commit a83fbae).
Network origins approved per package in widget_network_origins; install stores the version's origins (commit d6daf17).

Bounded upstream HTTP proxy with redirects not followed and a 4 s timeout (commit aacbbcb; moved to packages/contracts by 4932b12, see ev-later-commits), and the http.get and http.send gateway operations (commit 52ce207).
Install review shows network origins; widget UI maps UPSTREAM_ERROR to a message (commit 745b6ce).

Hermes Tasks widget package examples/widgets/hermes-tasks: pure modules for dates, views, quick add and layout (commit ed67b5c); Hermes Tasks client over the gateway (commit 7181bb6); autosave queue (commit 03be180); Vue UI with rail and stacked layouts, list, detail panel and toasts (commit e4a5c26); widget tests run outside dist (commit 387302f).

Post-acceptance fixes: quick add submits on Enter in the input, Esc closes the panel from anywhere in the frame, and a lost write keeps its retry (commit f66f225); gateway test pins for the timeout chain, send limit and origin rejection (commit 6accb6a); README origin wording (commit c5892fd).

risks.text: A listed hostname is resolved at request time, so DNS decides the address; the spec recommends IP literals, as Hermes Tasks uses 127.0.0.1.
A write whose answer is lost to a timeout may already have run upstream; the widget retries it with the same idempotency key.
Quick add, Esc and lost-write retry changed after the last recorded acceptance run and have no recorded browser result.

Later commits changed the gateway and widget beyond this feature: secret injection (1dade32, 1b0a9ae) and the proxy move (4932b12). This record covers the feature's own commits, not current gateway behaviour.

decisions.text: The API calls Hermes Tasks with Node fetch and the widget calls the gateway, because the sandbox origin is opaque and Hermes Tasks rejects Origin null with 403 ORIGIN_NOT_ALLOWED (checked 2026-10-11). Server-side requests send no Origin header and work in the Tauri build.

Generic HTTP proxy with an exact-origin allowlist per package, reviewed at install, so other widgets can reuse it. Origins are stored normalized with new URL(x).origin. Loopback and private hosts are allowed when listed and approved.
A new origin in a new package version is shown at install as a new permission, so a version never widens network access silently.
http.get is confirm never so polling never opens a dialog; http.send is confirm optional, so writes follow the grant mode (ask mode confirms each write).

Any upstream HTTP status is a successful gateway result, so the widget handles service errors such as 409 VERSION_CONFLICT itself. Redirects are not followed, because a redirect could leave the allowlist.
No secrets in this feature; Hermes Tasks on localhost needs no token.
Reschedule changes the current occurrence, not the series schedule; recurrence rules are shown read-only and changed through Hermes.
Widget tests use Vitest for pure modules only; the Vue components are checked in the browser against the live service.
